coordinator_review.objective_checked: Archive all twenty-one producer artifacts (15 IDEA records + 6 report/retrieval-screen files) before independent proposal review, and record any schema, novelty, cross-lane, or claim-ceiling defects found on an actual read of every artifact.
coordinator_review.artifact_count_check: PASS. Exactly 15 IDEA-* records exist at the declared paths (5 for RQ-QALG-457b41 under TASK-20260813-5bfa22, 5 for RQ-QALG-122b59 under TASK-20260813-9f7a4a, 5 for RQ-QALG-74bf20 under TASK-20260813-8dcf3d), plus the 6 declared idea-report.yaml/retrieval-screen.yaml producer artifacts (2 per task x 3 tasks) = 21 total, matching the batch's declared objective and this task's own artifact_paths list verbatim.

novelty_ceiling_check.detail: All 15 records set novelty_status: unverified with an explicit statement that crypto-kb MCP tools were unavailable in every one of the three producer sessions and that WebSearch failed on every attempted query in every session (a recorded backend/model error, not a zero-result search), per AGENTS.md rule 3/5 treated as infrastructure unavailability rather than novelty evidence. No record claims verified novelty, and no record treats absence of a corpus hit as evidence of novelty; several records say so explicitly (e.g. IDEA-20260813-e6d55d, IDEA-20260813-4aecda). This is honest and consistent across all three lanes.

cross_lane_inference_check.detail: Every record's interpretation_limits (or equivalent) section states explicitly that its findings do not transfer to the other two lanes, citing GOAL-QALG-001's own non_duplication note. The CSIDH lane's retrieval-screen.yaml (TASK-20260813-8dcf3d) contains an explicit cross_check_against_sibling_batch_lanes entry stating the ML-KEM and HQC producer dispatches were concurrent, separate, and NOT read or cited by this lane. No proposal in any lane cites a mechanism, cost figure, or finding from either of the other two lanes, or from GOAL-MLKEM-001/005 or GOAL-HQC-001's classical/DFR-model work, as load-bearing support for its own claim. Sibling references within the SAME lane (e.g. IDEA-20260813-c6e557 citing IDEA-20260813-55d3a0 and IDEA-20260813-e6d55d as orthogonal, both in the CSIDH lane) are in-lane and not a violation.

claim_ceiling_check.result: PASS, with one item flagged for the Validator's attention (not treated here as a violation).
claim_ceiling_check.detail: No record claims an approved experiment, an executed run, an official hypothesis-status transition, an evidence record, or a promotion. Every minimal_test/design block is explicit that it 'authorizes no execution' and is 'a design for Coordinator approval.' The HQC lane's three closure-shaped proposals (IDEA-20260813-a46301, IDEA-20260813-5a2aaa, IDEA-20260813-c34e09) use the phrase 'AUDIT PERFORMED, COLLISION FOUND' inside their proof_search_map.observation_collision fields. On inspection this refers to the cheap, pen-and-paper/symbolic pre-compute falsification checks that docs/inventor-protocol.md section 8 (KN-TECH-080) explicitly requires and authorizes AT IDEATION TIME -- e.g. IDEA-20260813-c34e09's audit is a one-line combinatorial/group-theory argument (orbit sizes under a free transitive Z_n action), and IDEA-20260813-5a2aaa's is an elementary F_2-linearity argument -- not an EXP-*/run-experiment execution, and no EXP-*, RUN-*, or EV-* id is referenced or implied. This is within the batch's ideation-only authorization and matches the batch's own required behavior ('a failed proof_search_map audit is itself a useful, recordable result', echoed in both idea-report.yaml files). Flagged here plainly so the independent Validator (TASK-20260813-520100) checks the same distinction explicitly rather than assuming it, since the phrase 'AUDIT PERFORMED' could be misread as claiming code was run.

schema_completeness_check.result: MIXED. All 15 records substantively cover the required content (mechanism, predictions, minimal_test, falsification_conditions, confounders, interpretation_limits, proof_search_map, target_complexity, heuristic_assumptions with validation_plan (or an explicit, argued reason none is needed), controls, dominated_by, sota_delta), but the three producer tasks used THREE DIFFERENT STRUCTURAL SCHEMAS for the same record type, which is flagged plainly rather than silently normalized.
schema_completeness_check.lane_1_ml_kem_task_5bfa22: Most complete: each record's `idea:` block carries a full header (id, added, proposed_by, status, question_id, goal_id), a structured `novelty_screen` mapping with five named subfields (local_kb_status, screened_proposals, adjacent_corpus, external_screen, nearest_neighbors), and `dominated_by`/`sota_delta`/`enumerated_closures`/`open_directions` nested inside the `idea:` block.
schema_completeness_check.lane_2_hqc_task_9f7a4a: STRUCTURALLY THINNER AND DIFFERENTLY SHAPED. IDEA-20260813-a46301, -5a2aaa, -c34e09, -319645, -fe3c5e omit `added`, `proposed_by`, `status`, `question_id`, and `goal_id` from the `idea:` block entirely -- the record cannot self-identify which research question or goal it belongs to without consulting the batch queue or the idea-report.yaml; this is a real cross-referencing gap the other two lanes do not have. `novelty_screen` is reduced to a bare `novelty_status: unverified` with no structured subfields; the equivalent narrative content instead lives in `object_first_screen` and `novelty_check` blocks placed OUTSIDE the `idea:` wrapper as top-level siblings, as are `dominated_by` and `sota_delta` -- a different location than lanes 1 and 3, where both are nested inside `idea:`. `enumerated_closures` and `open_directions` fields are absent at the record level (closure content exists only in prose inside `proof_search_map` and in the idea-report.yaml, not as a dedicated field).
schema_completeness_check.lane_3_csidh_task_8dcf3d: Intermediate: full header present (matches lane 1), but `novelty_screen` is a single narrative string rather than lane 1's structured five-subfield mapping; `dominated_by`/`sota_delta` are nested inside `idea:` (matches lane 1's placement, unlike lane 2); no `enumerated_closures`/`open_directions` fields at the record level (matches lane 2's gap, unlike lane 1).
schema_completeness_check.heuristic_assumptions_empty_list_note: IDEA-20260813-c34e09 and IDEA-20260813-319645 (both HQC lane) declare `heuristic_assumptions: []`. Both give an explicit, argued reason in-record: c34e09's claim is a deterministic, zero-sampling combinatorial fact (orbit-size divisibility) needing no heuristic; 319645's audit is recorded as inconclusive rather than resolved, and its own text does not supply a load-bearing heuristic beyond generic MNRS/electric-network equivalence. This is defensible on its face but is a literal reading against the batch.yaml constraint ('Every proposal must include ... heuristic assumptions and validation'), since an empty list is technically present-but-vacuous rather than populated. Flagged for the Validator to weigh, not resolved here.
schema_completeness_check.retrieval_screen_required_fields_note: batch.yaml declares `required_screen_fields: [query, query_id, source_id, chunk_id, content_hash, authority, claim_status, expanded_contexts]`, which is the schema of a crypto-kb MCP `search_knowledge` result. None of the three retrieval-screen.yaml files uses this field set even once, because crypto-kb MCP tools were unavailable in all three producer sessions (consistent with the operator's own recorded note that an unprovisioned kb/.env yields a server that never registers tools on this machine) and every producer substituted an ad hoc grep-based screening structure instead (each internally consistent and readable, but mutually different in field names across the three tasks: e.g. `candidate_mechanism_screens` in lane 1 vs `corpus_grep_queries` in lane 2 vs `per_idea_retrieval_trace` in lane 3). This is an infrastructure-driven gap between the batch's declared retrieval schema and what was actually deliverable, not a producer error, and is recorded here as a batch-level finding rather than charged against any one task.

coordinator_review.overall_assessment: The fifteen proposals are honest, internally consistent, and stay inside the batch's unverified-ideation claim ceiling: no verified-novelty claim, no cross-lane inference, no experiment/run/evidence/promotion language, and every closure-shaped or blocked-shaped result (HQC's two closures, the CSIDH lane's five NOT-EXECUTED-this-session audits, the ML-KEM lane's five design-stage-only proof_search_map passes) is reported plainly rather than inflated. The batch is READY for independent Validator review (TASK-20260813-520100) AS-IS, on the content and claim-ceiling merits. It is NOT schema-uniform: the HQC lane (task 9f7a4a) uses a materially different and, on net, thinner record structure than its two siblings (missing self-identifying header fields; dominated_by/sota_delta/novelty detail relocated outside the idea: block; no enumerated_closures/open_directions field), and the batch's own declared retrieval_screen field schema was never actually usable given crypto-kb's unavailability. Both points are handed to the Validator explicitly above rather than silently normalized or treated as blocking; neither is a claim-ceiling or novelty-ceiling violation, and neither, in this reviewer's judgment, requires returning the batch to the Idea Generator before independent review, since the substantive content the batch.yaml constraint actually requires (proof_search_map, target complexity, heuristic assumptions and validation or an argued absence, controls, falsification, dominated_by, sota_delta) is present in every one of the 15 records under some field name or placement.
